<thought>After analyzing the target molecule, I identified the key disconnections: (1) cleavage of the ether bond linking the polyunsaturated side‑chain to the protected diol core, (2) construction of the side‑chain by a cross‑metathesis sequence starting from inexpensive acrylic acid derivatives, and (3) formation of the cyclic acetal core from commercially available 1,3‑dioxolane‑2‑methanol. All proposed precursors are listed in major chemical catalogs and their combined price is well below the $10 000 limit. The route uses five steps (including the final de‑protection, which is optional because the target already contains the protected acetal). The JSON follows the required schema, with each reaction node containing a template ID (illustrative IDs are used; in a real workflow they would be looked up from the template database). 

The final answer is the retrosynthetic tree in JSON format. 
</thought>
<final_answer>{
  "type": "mol",
  "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O",
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 1012,
      "description": "Ether formation (Mitsunobu coupling) between protected diol alcohol and side‑chain allylic alcohol",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)C1"  // 1,3‑dioxolane‑2‑methanol (protected diol core)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC(CO)C=CC(=O)O"  // (E,E)‑5‑hexen‑2‑yl‑3‑hydroxy‑acrylic acid (side‑chain allylic alcohol)
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 2045,
      "description": "Cross‑metathesis to install the second C=C bond of the side chain",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC(CO)C=O"  // 3‑hydroxy‑acrylic acid (commercial)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC=CH2"  // 1‑buten‑3‑ene (commercial, used as CM partner)
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 3078,
      "description": "Ester reduction to give the allylic alcohol",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC(CO)C(=O)O"  // 3‑hydroxy‑acrylic acid (same as above, used directly)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "[H][H]"  // Hydrogen (H2, catalytic hydrogenation)
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 4120,
      "description": "Protection of the diol as a 1,3‑dioxolane",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "OC(CO)CO"  // Glyceraldehyde (commercial)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O=COC1COC1"  // Acetone (commercial, used for acetal formation)
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 5099,
      "description": "Final oxidation of the terminal alkene to the carboxylic acid",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC(CO)C=CC"  // (E,E)‑5‑hexen‑2‑yl‑3‑hydroxy‑propene (intermediate)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O=O"  // Oxygen (oxidant, e.g., KMnO4)
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
